name: Four-role atmospheric pad with air built in at the source: low-passed low wavetable layer, high-passed harsh high layer an octave up on an unsynced morph rate, an unfiltered octave-up triangle for tone, and a key-tracked noise sample through the same high-pass; then chorus, a little phaser/flanger, ping-pong delay, reverb and EQ placement
goal: Beyond 'attack + release + unison + reverb': split one patch into roles. Osc 1 low layer (smooth wavetable, position on a 1-bar LFO, unison, attack, low-pass). Osc 2 high layer (harsh/digital wavetable +1 octave, position LFO at a free rate in seconds so it never morphs in step with osc 1, unison, through a HIGH-PASS so only its upper harmonics remain: this is the air). Osc 3 triangle +1 octave with unison, unfiltered, carries the pitch. Noise/sample osc: a steady broadband recording (e.g. a box fan) with key tracking ON, pitched to match osc 3, through the high-pass. Balance levels, then chorus, phaser and flanger mixed in lightly (flanger feedback down), ping-pong delay with one side at 1/4, a long large reverb, EQ to place the pad high or low. Macro the unison detune of all three oscillators.

source.title: How to Create Unique PADS in VITAL, Serum and Phaseplant

prerequisites: A multi-oscillator wavetable synth with a sample/noise oscillator and two filters (Vital is free)
Chorus, phaser, flanger, delay, reverb, EQ

outputs.name: pad
outputs.description: Atmospheric pad with built-in air layer

constraints: Wavetable-position LFOs move timbre only, never pitch; the free-rate LFO is a steady periodic LFO (not random/S&H).
Phaser/flanger mixed low as colour, not a sweeping effect; no rapid clicking textures.
Noise layer must be key-tracked so its colour follows the chord.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Osc 1 (low layer): choose a smooth wavetable, LFO 1 (1 bar) -> wavetable position, add unison and a slow attack, send to filter 1 low-pass and bring the cutoff down.

Osc 2 (high layer): choose a harsh/digital wavetable with rich highs, +1 octave, LFO 2 -> position at a free rate in seconds (not tempo-synced) so it morphs out of step with osc 1, unison, send to filter 2 set to HIGH-PASS.
Osc 3 (tonal layer): basic triangle, +1 octave, unison, bypass the filters.
steps.expect: Clear pitch centre that backs the other layers

steps.action: Noise/sample osc: load a steady broadband sample (e.g. box fan), turn keyboard tracking on and tune it to osc 3, route through the high-pass filter.
Balance the four layers; the high layer may sound piercing alone but sits once blended.
FX: chorus; then a phaser and a flanger mixed in a little (flanger feedback down).
Ping-pong delay with one side at 1/4, then a long, large reverb with mix up; skip the reverb filter.
EQ to place the pad (cut lows for a high pad, cut highs for a deep pad); if still too bright/tonal/noisy, rebalance the source layers.
steps.expect: Pad fits its slot in the track

steps.action: Map one macro to the unison detune of oscs 1-3 for later tweaking.

verification: Spectral centroid of the full pad is higher than the low layer alone, and the high layer alone has little energy below its HP cutoff.
Noise layer pitch follows the played chord (key tracking on).
Osc 1 and osc 2 position LFO rates are not integer-related to the tempo pair (they drift apart).
No pitch modulation on any oscillator; peak below 0 dBFS.
